en:
I see. Just as the Captain said,
this is one strange ruin. You
want us to investigate the
place, right?

I may not possess the same
level of knowledge as the
Federation authorities, but... if
this is similar to the Cursed
Seal Temple on planet
Faykreed, I believe I can be of
use.

I don't really get it, so I'll leave
the investigating to you two. In
exchange, leave the enemies
on the way to me!

I'm counting on you, young lady.
Now, Erys... that was it, right?
It feels a bit strange that you
have the same name as my
daughter.
Oh, really? What a curious\ncoincidence. It's nice to meet\nyou properly, mister.
...Hey now, do I really look that\nold? Well, anyway, glad to be\nworking with you.

Hehe... This is the first time I'll
be working with you as well. It
is a pleasure to meet you, Ms.
Erys and Mr. Bowman.
Yeah, likewise. Now, let's see...
This is Raffine, the Healer.
This is Raffine, the researcher\nfrom Kronos.
Uh... who was she again?

Ah, and you're the one! I've
heard all about you. You're the
one who's been helping the
Captain and the others since
the crew was still small, right?
You're a researcher from\nKronos, right? You seem smart.

Ah... I've heard about you from
the Faykreed folks. You're a
researcher in Symbology,
specializing in biology, right?

You were a precious healer
back when the crew was still
small, weren't you? So, you're a
doctor who also does
research?

...From the Federation's
perspective, I'm from a frontier
region and a rival organization.
It's only natural that I'd be
forgotten. ...Um, my name is
Raffine.

Oh, you're Raffine! You were a
precious healer back when the
crew was still small, weren't
you? How cruel of the Captain
to forget you.

Ah... I've heard about you from
the Faykreed folks. You're a
researcher in Symbology,
specializing in biology, right?

...My research is nothing to be
proud of. Nor is it something I
need to hide at this point. That
is why I am the right person
for this facility's research.

Facing the past and its
possibilities can be painful for
some. But as for me... we had
no other choice.
That is why... no matter what I\nsee, I will feel neither regret\nnor pain.

...Ah, I thought so. That's inside
the Kronos Central Symbology
Research Institute. From when
they came to retrieve Felria...
Relia's other half...
And you are?
I am Raffine. The administrator\nof the biological research\nsector of this institute.
Please, come with me. I will\nlead you to the child.
Wait. Why are you cooperating\nwith us?
Because... you were strong.
Strong?
Not every researcher in this\nsector is happy with the\ncurrent research.
We don't want to involve those\ntwo in this plan any longer.
However, simply freeing them\nwould only mean they'd be\nhunted forever.
We need someone capable of\nprotecting them from both\nKronos and the Federation.
Now, this way.

I know this is forward of me,
but I beg you. Please free
those two from being used as
tools of war.

...We in Kronos feared the
immense power of the Galactic
Federation after our first
contact 16 years ago.

Thus, to weaponize our
superior symbol science and
technology, we began
large-scale practical research
on spatiotemporal symbol
creatures.

Many test subjects were
created, but only two
successfully took hold. Only
Relia, whom you know, and a
girl named Felria.

You're so kind, Raffine. You
were willing to betray your own
country just to save those
girls, weren't you?

I am not kind... It was we
researchers who created them
as space-time sigil creatures in
the first place.

...Being a government scholar is
rough. Forced to do things
against your will. But it's hard
to chase an ideal when it
means throwing away your
livelihood.
Even so, by cooperating with\nother researchers, we managed\nto let Relia escape via shuttle.

As for Felria, whom we couldn't
get away... in the end, we failed
to save her. The scene you
saw earlier was eventually
discovered by the higher-ups.

I am nothing like the heroes
who saved the universe... The
most I can save is one person...
then and now.
But even if it was only one... I\nam still happy that I was able\nto save Relia.

O-oh, that reminds me... You
betrayed your country, right?
What happened to you and the
others after that...?

You said you only saved one
person... Y-you just aren't
counting yourselves, right?
Surely you don't mean only one
person in total...?

Kronos was a harsh
organization. ...I wanted to do
something for the subordinates
who acted as parents to those
girls, but...

...My current surroundings are
like heaven. I don't think I'll
encounter any more sadness...
like having to hesitate to
embrace someone during a
final farewell.

For the sake of the Captain,
who is the heart of it all, and
to protect the ship, I will do my
absolute best. I'll give it
everything I've got.

The exploration tips I got from
Ernest really paid off. There's a
Gem under the dust. Could you
take a look, Raffine?

As I thought, this is from the
Cursed Temple... I'll
cross-reference it with the
Quad Scanner I borrowed from
Coro.

Those two... after seeing that
kind of past, how can they just
calmly investigate and
exchange opinions? I'd expect
a bit more conflict, or at least
some hesitation...
Because they're adults.
Because they're scholars.
Maybe they're just Still\nWaters?
Do you have something on your\nmind?
...I see. 27 and 29. I guess\nthey've outgrown the kind of\nconflict you find in youth.
I wonder if the Captain is the\nsame way?
...Scholars are amazing. It's a\nkind of gift, a Talent.

...I see, Still Waters. No silence,
no confusion... in many ways,
they're just not affected by
the poison...
N-no, I don't. I just wonder how\nI'd react, or rather, I'm here\nknowing full well what it's like...
...Honestly, there's nothing else!\nI said there's nothing!

...Hey, Professor Bowman.
Aren't you afraid? Having other
people see your past or your
possibilities?

As long as it ain't somethin' I
couldn't show a child, I ain't too
worried. I've already shared
most of it with Claude and my
wife.
...You're strong. The Erys in\nyour world is lucky to have\nsuch a strong father.
I guess. Not that... it means the\npain doesn't hurt, though.
...I can see it. Is that the town\nof Linga...? No, it's the port\ntown of Harlee.

If so, this is when I went to get
the medicinal herb Metox for a
girl with a severe illness... right
as I was returning.
Ma'am! How is your daughter's\ncondition?
Mother: Oh, it's terrible! She...\nshe suddenly collapsed!
Mother: Please! Help my\ndaughter... help Elanor!
Gah!? She's already fallen into\na coma...
This illness should be cured if I\nuse the medicine made from\nthis Metox.
However...
However? What is it?
That is, provided the girl still\nhas enough strength left in\nher...
What!?
Given the current situation, I'd\nsay it's a fifty-fifty chance.

This Aialo disease apparently
progresses slowly, so she could
likely survive another year as
she is.
One year...

But... if her frail body cannot
withstand the potency of the
medicine, she might die as
soon as tomorrow.

Of course, if we don't
administer the medicine
immediately, her chances of
recovery will continue to
dwindle...
You must decide, Mother. Do\nyou let your daughter live out a\nlimited life of only one year?
Or do you take the risk and\ngamble on her future...
Mother: Ah! I can't... I can't\nmake such a terrifying choice!
It's only natural. Her daughter's\nlife is on the line, after all...
Claude, you decide.
What... but why!?
I know what you're trying to\nsay. But...

A mother's heart cannot bear
the weight of the guilt that
comes with choosing to let her
own daughter die.
She needs someone else to\nshoulder the responsibility.
I understand...
...T-this! It's so... cruel... Kuro...\nBut still...

Miss Erys, you don't have to
force yourself to say anything.
This is a situation where there
is no right answer.

I feel bad for forcing such a
heavy choice upon Claude, who
isn't even a doctor and simply
brought the herbs...

But there was no one else
suited for it... Now, what was it
that Claude decided in the
end...?
I think it's better to bet on the\npossibility.
I'll give it everything I've got for\na year.
Ah, that's right, that's right.\nLook... the scene is playing\nback in my mind.
It would be better for this girl\nto bet on a possibility than to\nsurvive in constant agony.
I can't just let her die in vain.\nHer life has only just begun...
I feel the same way.
You're okay with that too,\naren't you, ma'am?
Mother: Yes... please, I leave it\nto you.
All right! From here on, it's my\njob as a doctor.
What!? But...
A human life is far heavier than\nyou think.
Far too heavy for you to carry\nall on your own...
Bowman...
Ah, that's right. Look... the\nscene is playing back.
If she had a year, this girl\ncould surely leave something\nbehind for the world.
We can't take such a\ndangerous gamble. The odds\nare far too poor.
It's unfortunate, but all we can\ndo now is let her live her\nremaining year to the fullest.
I see... you might be right.
You agree with that, don't you,\nma'am?
Mother: ...Yes...
Huh!? Mom...?
Mother: *Sob*... Elanor...
What's wrong? Why are you\ncrying?
Mr. Bowman. We're just so\npowerless, aren't we...?

Well... when you've been in this
profession as long as I have,
you learn that these things
happen. You did your best.
Keep your head up...

...She was saved, right? This
child was actually saved? It
would be cruel if we went
through the trouble of
gathering herbs only for her to
die!

Well, in medicine, there are
things that just can't be done
no matter how hard you try. In
the end, it comes down to luck.

Unless there's someone willing
to take that bad luck upon
themselves. Well, the day will
come when you see the
outcome.

...Life can be turned to ash so
easily... yet saving a life on the
brink of extinction is so
difficult...

...It's too late to hide it from
you all now, Captain. I... I have
a past where I was
brainwashed and worked as an
assassin.

...That must have been so
painful. Are you sure you're
okay with us seeing those
memories of your past...?

To be honest, I thought about
watching it alone... just to
remind myself of what I've
done.

If I don't take opportunities like
this, I feel like I'll get swept up
in how happy you all are and
forget my sins.
But...

...Sinking into solitary reflection
isn't exactly healthy. If it's a
matter of watching and
remembering together, I'm in.
He's right. Please don't worry.\nWe could never hate you.
Thank you... All right then...\nlook. This is... my past!

I wonder which town that is?
Was it during one of the
assassinations? Or the town
where people threw stones at
me after my memories
returned...?
Woof woof! Woof woof woof!
...Eh? A dog barking? Was\nthere ever a dog at the\nscene...? Oh, is Lati there too?
Dog: Whine, whine...
Girl: Hey, stop barking! This\nperson isn't bad!
Y-yeah, exactly, we're not bad\npeople...
Dog: Grrr... Woof woof woof\nwoof!
Girl: Oh, stop it!
...Lati, are you afraid of dogs?
No, I actually like them... but\nanyone would be startled if one\nbarked at them, right?
Dogs are just judging whether\nsomeone is a threat to their\nowner.
Dog: Grrr...
See, I'm not an enemy~.
Dog: Grrr, grrr...
Do you want to be turned to\nash?
Dog: Yip... yip yip!
See? Some things can be\ncommunicated just through the\natmosphere.
...Huh?
Miss Erys...?

T-That's a mistake! That was
some kind of mistake! Now,
play something more
appropriate, you ruins!
Really? Gray is a lovely color.
...Watching evil monsters turn\nto ash is so satisfying.\n...Hehehehe...
Hey, I heard you were going to\ndraw a portrait of me...
I see... so now you're ignoring\nme too...?
...Hehe... Ahaha! What is this? Is\nthis some kind of penalty\ngame?
Let's turn these ruins to ash.\nThey're already gray, so it's\nperfect.

C-Calm down, we aren't going
to hate you for this. ...Though I
am starting to reconsider the
name for my daughter.

Exactly. It's obvious what her
personality is like just by
watching her. It's a bit late for
that now...!
Just turn into ash, all of you!

This story has come to an end.
More stories will be released in
the future, so please look
forward to them.
